If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract overconfidence bias.

If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and forecast is trending upward, apply a 1–2% downward correction in late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overextension.

When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecast starting from day 7 onward.

If sentiment is consistently positive over 7 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for all horizons to reflect diminishing momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative over 7 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to offset pessimism bias.
